beats.care: Grids everywhere, including India's, run on a fine balance. As more homes add solar, keeping that balance gets trickier.
beats.what: Sri Lanka's power went out across the island around noon on Saturday and came back in stages over more than three hours.
beats.why: The grid operator called it a total system failure. The energy minister pointed to a breakdown at the Upper Kotmale hydropower station.

cards.body: A grid must match supply and demand every second. If a big plant suddenly drops out, frequency falls, and other plants trip to protect themselves, like dominoes.
cards.title: how can one fault black out a country?

cards.body: It's Sri Lanka's second islandwide blackout in under two years. In February 2025, a minister blamed a monkey at a substation.
Mobile networks and water supply were hit too, since pumps and towers need power. The government said a hydro station failure found on Friday may have played a part.

opts: Other plants trip in a chain to protect themselves
cards.q: Why can a single plant failure black out a whole grid?
cards.why: Losing a big plant throws supply off balance, and protective shutdowns spread like dominoes.

hook: A whole country went dark at noon. *What breaks a national grid?*

learn.t: When a grid fails, rooftop solar owners are told to disconnect, because sudden extra power can destabilise it while it restarts.
